items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 16:1
items.html: (To the question) These seven aspects that the Rav counts include all the changes of the principal states that there are in the Nukva. For first he counts the Ibur, Yenika, and Mochin of the posterior, which are the first three aspects. Then he counts the fourth aspect, which is the Yenika of the front. Then he counts the two aspects of the Mochin of Aba and Ima and of YESHSUT: the Mochin of YESHSUT of the front he counts as the fifth degree, and the Mochin of the front from Aba and Ima he counts as the sixth degree; and both of them using a single Keter face to face he counts as the seventh degree. (Item 108).
